subject: Educational Psychology
stem: Bruner's famous, and initially controversial, hypothesis states that:

options.option_text: Any subject can be taught effectively in some intellectually honest form to any child at any stage of development
Children cannot learn abstract concepts until formal operational stage (age 11+)
Only gifted children can learn complex subjects before adolescence
Readiness for learning is fixed entirely by biological maturation

explanation: Bruner's readiness hypothesis challenged the Piagetian view that children must wait for a maturational stage before learning certain concepts — instead arguing that any idea can be presented in a developmentally appropriate (enactive/iconic/symbolic) form even to young children.
